author: EmuCore - Hub
title: What's BETTER? Software Rendering OR Vulkan? (PCSX2 Emulation) - Affro's Curiosities
summary: Affro contrasts PCSX2 software rendering with Vulkan across more than twenty PS2 games, using one documented emulator build to explore the practical exchange between closer GS behavior, higher internal resolution and game-specific faults.

blocks.text: The twenty-six-minute test spans effects-heavy action, racers, fighters and horror games instead of choosing a renderer from a single success case. PCSX2 1.7.2641 is identified, Vulkan targets 1080p internal resolution, and both PAL and NTSC software appear. Software mode supplies a useful lower-level reference for scenes that hardware rendering mishandles, while Vulkan demonstrates the clarity and throughput available when the host GPU reconstructs the workload. The many chaptered titles reveal that renderer choice is often per game and sometimes per scene.

Software rendering is not automatically identical to a retail PS2, and Vulkan at higher resolution changes more than the graphics API. The recording mixes regions and uses an old development build, ShadowPlay capture and a 4K export, so differences cannot be assigned to one variable with laboratory precision. Its value is comparative breadth and visible failure discovery. Confirm a suspected issue on a current build, match internal resolution where possible, record frame pacing, and test the same save state before deciding which backend is more faithful or faster.
